summary: Frontend-only test of Sertex Tasks 3-dot menu redesign (right-click deprecated as primary path). 3-dot button is now always visible (opacity 1), 32x32, cyan-bordered, at the right edge of every task card — verified visually and via computed style. All 14 functional flows pass when the menu is exercised via JS click: pending task shows [Tamamlandı, Beklemeye al, Sil] (ctx-pending hidden as required); ctx-paused → yellow bg + BEKLEMEDE badge; ctx-pending on paused task → yellow/badge removed; ctx-done → emerald bg + strikethrough title; ctx-delete removes the task; Escape closes; outside-click closes; hint text updated to 'Kartın sağındaki ⋮ butonuna tıklayarak durumu değiştir' with no right-click mention; regression: add task + checkbox toggle-to-done still work. HOWEVER — CRITICAL VISUAL BUG discovered: after clicking the 3-dot button the context menu opens OFFSCREEN. Its inline style is left:1704px top:290px (correct viewport-space math) but getBoundingClientRect returns left:3245 (viewport width is 1920). Root cause: <aside data-testid='sidebar'> has backdrop-filter: blur(16px) via the .glass-panel class. Per CSS spec, a non-none backdrop-filter on an ancestor establishes a containing block for descendants with position: fixed. So the menu's left:1704 is interpreted relative to the sidebar (whose left edge is ~1540px) → real x ≈ 1540+1704 = 3244 → completely offscreen to the right. Playwright's real .click() on ctx-* buttons even fails with 'Element is outside of the viewport' — that IS the exact user experience: users click the 3-dot button and see NOTHING. The right-click path (setCtx from e.clientX/e.clientY) is broken by the same containing-block issue and was likely reported as passing in iter_6 only because the previous agent checked DOM presence, not visual placement.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: Context menu renders completely offscreen (~x=3245 in a 1920px viewport) when opened via the 3-dot button. Root cause: the parent <aside data-testid='sidebar'> uses backdrop-filter: blur(16px) (via .glass-panel), which per CSS spec establishes a new containing block for position:fixed descendants. As a result the menu's left:1704px is computed relative to the sidebar's left edge (~1540px), not the viewport. User-visible symptom: clicking the 3-dot ⋮ button appears to do nothing — no menu is visible anywhere on screen. This defeats the entire purpose of this iteration (making the 3-dot button the primary way to open the menu).

Same containing-block bug also breaks the right-click flow. e.clientX/e.clientY are viewport coords but get treated as sidebar-relative once inserted into a position:fixed element inside the backdrop-filtered aside — so right-click menus also appear offscreen. Previous iteration_6 report said right-click 'works' but that was DOM-existence only.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): Portal the ContextMenu out of the sidebar's backdrop-filter subtree. Cleanest fix: wrap the returned <motion.div ...data-testid='task-context-menu'> inside ReactDOM.createPortal(<motion.div .../>, document.body). This escapes the sidebar's containing-block so position:fixed with left/top actually uses the viewport. Alternative: change the menu's positioning to relative-to-button using position:absolute inside a small position:relative wrapper on the TaskCard (avoids fixed altogether). Do NOT remove backdrop-filter from the sidebar — it's used elsewhere for the glass style.

AFTER FIX: Re-verify by clicking the 3-dot on any task and confirming (a) getBoundingClientRect().left of task-context-menu equals its style left, and (b) the menu is visually on screen next to the button. Then re-run steps 7–13 with real Playwright .click() (not JS click) to ensure the menu is inside the viewport.
critical_code_review_comments: ContextMenu.js line ~105 style={{ left: Math.min(x, window.innerWidth - 200), top: Math.min(y, window.innerHeight - 200) }} — clamping assumes viewport-relative positioning, which is invalidated the moment any ancestor gains transform/filter/backdrop-filter/perspective/contain/will-change:transform. In this app the sidebar has backdrop-filter: blur(16px), so the whole clamp is meaningless. Portal to body to make this contract hold.

TaskCard 3-dot onClick sets ctx to { x: rect.left - 160, y: rect.bottom + 4 } using viewport coords from getBoundingClientRect. This is the correct math for a body-portal-mounted menu; combined with the current in-place render inside the sidebar it produces the observed 1541px horizontal drift.
The useEffect cleanup in ContextMenu now correctly removes BOTH mousedown and keydown listeners — good fix from previous iteration.
Existing right-click handler (onContextMenu) uses e.clientX/e.clientY — same viewport-coordinate assumption; will start working correctly the moment the menu is portaled to document.body.
isOverdue is recomputed on every render — fine for now, but if the task list grows large consider memoizing.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The 3-dot menu ONLY appears to work in DOM-level assertions — visually the menu is offscreen. Any future test MUST either (a) take a screenshot right after opening the menu and assert its bounding-box is inside the viewport, or (b) verify getBoundingClientRect().left of task-context-menu equals its inline style left. Do NOT rely on JS-based .click() to prove the flow works, because that hides the offscreen positioning. Root cause is the .glass-panel backdrop-filter on <aside data-testid='sidebar'>. Fix will most likely be a React portal in the ContextMenu component; once shipped, the same test script here will pass with normal Playwright .click() too.
rca of the issue: CSS spec (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_positioned_layout/Understanding_z-index/The_stacking_context and https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Containing_block#identifying_the_containing_block): position:fixed elements are normally positioned relative to the viewport, UNLESS an ancestor has any of {transform, filter, backdrop-filter, perspective, will-change: transform, contain: paint/layout/strict/content} set to a non-initial value. In that case, the closest such ancestor becomes the containing block. The sidebar aside has backdrop-filter: blur(16px) (Tailwind class inside .glass-panel), so it becomes the containing block for the ContextMenu. The 3-dot button code computes menu position with getBoundingClientRect (viewport coords: rect.left-160 ≈ 1704), so it places the menu at 'left: 1704px' assuming viewport relativity — but the actual containing block is the sidebar whose left edge is at ~1540. Result: real render position is ~3245px, ~1300px past the right edge of a 1920 viewport. Reproduction: log in → Görevler tab → click ⋮ on any task → menu is present in DOM but invisible. Mitigation: React portal the ContextMenu to document.body (or absolutely position it inside a relative wrapper on the TaskCard). Verified via getBoundingClientRect returning left=3245 while inline style left=1704px and every ancestor computed style transform='none'; only backdrop-filter='blur(16px)' was non-initial in the chain.
